## Data: Sleep Study

Today, we will study the `sleepstudy` dataset (included in `lmerTest` package), which includes *real* data from a 2003 study (Belensky et al. 2003) on the relationship between sleep deprivation and reaction time. 18 subjects participated for 10 total days:

- Day 0: Subjects got a regular night's sleep
- Days 1--9: Subjects were restricted to 3 hours of sleep per night.

On each day, the researchers recorded the reaction times of the subjects in milliseconds, on a series of tests. You will model the relationship between `Reaction` time and `Days` of the experiment. Run the code chunk below to load the data and display two exploratory plots (notice how they display side-by-side!)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data("sleepstudy") # load the data
plot1 <- ggplot(sleepstudy,aes(x=Reaction))+ # saving 1st ggplot
  geom_histogram(bins=20,color="white")+theme_bw()
plot2 <- ggplot(sleepstudy,aes(x=Days,y=Reaction,color=Subject))+ # saving 2nd ggplot
  geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:9)+theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position="bottom")+guides(color=guide_legend(nrow=3))
grid.arrange(plot1,plot2,nrow=1,widths=c(.4,.6)) # arranging two ggplots side-by-side
```

## 3 Candidate Models

We would like to compare three models:

1.  Fixed Effects (`model_fe`): Reaction by Days (fixed effect) + Subject (fixed effects)
2.  Random Intercepts (`model_ri`): Reaction by Days (fixed effect) and Subject (random effects)
3.  Random Slopes (`model_rs`): Reaction by Days (fixed and random effects) and Subject (random effects)

Note: **Reaction times across days are inherently correlated within subject!** Thus, the fixed effects model violates the independence assumption and is *wrong!!* We study it here *only for illustration*.

### Question 4 (Plotting Models)

In the code chunk below, edit the code to plot each model on the data.

(i) For fixed effects plot, `FE`, add on `geom_parallel_slopes(se=F)`
(ii) For random intercepts and slopes plots, `RI` and `RS`, use `geom_abline()` (see slides)

What do you notice? Which model would you prefer?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
FE <- ggplot(sleepstudy,aes(x=Days,y=Reaction,color=Subject))+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position = "none")+labs(title="Fixed Effects")+
  geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:9)

RI <- ggplot(sleepstudy,aes(x=Days,y=Reaction,color=Subject))+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position = "none")+labs(title="Random Intercepts")+
  geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:9)

RS <- ggplot(sleepstudy,aes(x=Days,y=Reaction,color=Subject))+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position = "none")+labs(title="Random Slopes")+
  geom_point()+scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:9)

## Code below displays a plot grid
grid.arrange(FE,RI,RS,nrow=2)
```
